title: A finite type sheaf lives on a finitely presented closed subscheme with prescribed fibre support
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a finite type morphism [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] of affine schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-affine-spectrum], let $\mathcal F$ be a finite-type quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module [pqf-def-coherent], and let $x\in X$, $s=f(x)$. Write $X_s=X\times_S\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$ [def-pc-fibre-product, def-weil-residue-field] and let $\mathcal F_s$ be the pullback of $\mathcal F$ to $X_s$ [def-pc-module-pullback]. There exist a closed immersion $j:Z\to X$ of finite presentation [def-weil-closed-immersion, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation] and a finite-type quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_Z$-module $\mathcal H$ such that $j_*\mathcal H\cong\mathcal F$ and the underlying closed subset $|Z\times_S\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)|$ of $|X_s|$ equals $\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal F_s)=\{u\in X_s:(\mathcal F_s)_u\ne0\}$, with $(\mathcal F_s)_u$ the stalk [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk]. Here $j_*\mathcal H(V)=\mathcal H(j^{-1}V)$ for open subsets $V\subseteq X$.

proof.text: Put B=Γ(X,O_X), M=Γ(X,F), and I=Ann_B(M). The affine support theorem, applied to the top affine open of X, gives Supp(F)=X.zeroLocus(I). In Lean this is support_eq_zeroLocus_top, obtained directly from finite_type_module_support_closed and IsAffineOpen.fromSpec_image_zeroLocus; no explicit replacement of F by a tilde is necessary.

Let T=X×_S Spec κ(f(x)) and g:T→X be the first projection. Since f is a morphism of affine schemes, T is affine. The second projection is locally of finite type over the spectrum of a field; hence T is locally Noetherian and R=Γ(T,O_T) is Noetherian (Mathlib AlgebraicGeometry.Noetherian, using the affine finite-type ring criterion and finite-type-over-a-field Noetherianity). Write φ=g.appTop:B→R. The support-pullback theorem gives Supp(g*F)=g⁻¹(Supp(F)), and preimage_zeroLocus identifies g⁻¹(V(K)) with V(K.map φ) for every ideal K of B.

The ideal I.map φ is finitely generated since R is Noetherian. The finite-subset-of-a-span lemma chooses a finite subset of φ(I) spanning this ideal. Choose a preimage in I for each element of that finite set, and let J be their span in B. This explicitly gives J finitely generated, J⊆I, and J.map φ=I.map φ (the private proved helper exists_fg_subideal_map_eq). Equality of these mapped ideals gives g⁻¹(V(J))=g⁻¹(V(I)). The finite set may be empty; the construction also covers the zero ring.

Let K be the ideal sheaf IdealSheafData.ofIdealTop J and take Z=K.subscheme and j=K.subschemeι. The affine ideal/closed-subscheme dictionary gives that j is a closed immersion with range V(J). Its affine ideals are images of J and hence finitely generated, so the proved source-library lemma IdealSheafData.locallyOfFinitePresentation_subschemeι gives local finite presentation; closed immersions are quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Form the ideal sheaf A with A(U)=Ann(F(U)); annihilator_affine_basicOpen supplies its compatibility. Since X is affine and J⊆Ann(M), comparison on global sections gives K≤A, so K(U) kills F(U) on every affine open. Apply the proved source-library theorem isIso_pullbackUnit_subschemeι_of_smul_eq_zero to get F≅j_*j^*F. Define H=tensorPullback j F. Uniqueness of left adjoints compares this pullback with the library pullback used by that theorem. The pullback finite-type and quasi-coherence theorems give these properties of H; transport the preceding isomorphism to j_*H≅F. This is exactly the quotient-module construction of Stacks 057Q, packaged by the existing pullback-unit API.

For the exact canonical pullback.map appearing in the statement, Scheme.Pullback.range_map identifies its range with g⁻¹(range j), since the other two maps are identities. The point-existence theorem for scheme pullbacks underlies this range calculation. Substituting range j=V(J), equality J.map φ=I.map φ, Supp(F)=V(I), and Supp(g*F)=g⁻¹(Supp(F)) proves the required support equality. This avoids explicit tensor-product quotient and tilde-pullback identifications.

tool_uses.why: Affine finite-type ring-map characterization needed to pass from the morphism hypothesis to A→B finite type; this trace-formula unit has no such algebra lemma.
Affine quasi-coherent finite-type modules correspond to finite modules and provide the finite-type sheaf H; this is a generic affine module tool.
Affine support equals the annihilator zero locus for F; this generic support theorem is not supplied by the trace-formula unit.
The fibre support is the inverse image of Supp(F) under pullback; the unit has no fibre-support comparison theorem.
A finite-type algebra over a field is Noetherian, so the fibre extension ideal has finitely many generators; this algebra theorem is outside the unit route.
Step 2 identifies the fibre module F_s with the tilde of M⊗_Aκ(p); this affine pullback formula is a generic module tool not supplied by the trace-formula unit (added by the maintainer reader).
